record.paper_title: Doubly-Special Relativity: First Results and Key Open Problems
record.original_question: What should count as a DSR observer, and how should observer-dependent measurements be modeled when the theory may require macroscopic observers using different kinds of probes? The paper suggests that Planck-scale deformation may not apply to the observer as a macroscopic system and that high-energy probes could alter perceived time dilation, length contraction, and related measurements. The unresolved problem is to give a genuine description of DSR observers and determine, in particular, whether the relation between rapidity and relative velocity remains the special-relativistic one or must itself be modified.

evidence.quote: It appears likely that the theory will require the obsever to be a macroscopic system, to which the Planck-scale deformation does not apply. Since we lack a description of macroscopic bodies, we are also still lacking a genuine understanding of DSR obsevers.
For example, in a context probed with high-energy probes the observer might experience a different type of time dilatation and leangth contraction. But this has not yet been investigated.

At the merely technical level these issues concerning the DSR observer are relevant for establishing the relation between rapidity and relative velocity among observers. Is this relation modified? Or should we still adopt the special-relativistic relation between rapidity and relative velocity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Doubly Special Relativity (DSR) is a proposed framework that deforms special relativity by introducing, in addition to the invariant speed of light c, a second observer-independent scale (typically identified with the Planck energy E_p or Planck length L_p). In DSR the linear Lorentz transformations between inertial observers are replaced by nonlinear, energy-dependent deformations of boosts, while preserving the relativity principle.

Within this framework, formulate a precise notion of a "DSR observer" satisfying the following desiderata:

1. The observer is a macroscopic measuring system (composed of many quanta with individual energies far below E_p), so that the Planck-scale deformation that applies to elementary probes should not, naively, apply to the observer itself as a whole. Provide a consistent rule that specifies how the deformed boost generators act on (i) elementary high-energy probes and (ii) composite macroscopic observers, in a way compatible with the relativity principle and with the absence of detectable Planck-scale effects on macroscopic bodies.

2. Using this rule, model an observer-dependent measurement when the probes used by the observer have energies comparable to E_p. In particular, derive the expressions, in DSR, for:
   (a) time dilation,
   (b) length contraction,
   as functions of the relative motion between two macroscopic observers and of the energies of the probes used to perform the measurements.

3. Determine the relation between rapidity ξ and the relative velocity v between two DSR observers. Concretely, decide whether the special-relativistic identification v/c = tanh(ξ) survives in DSR, or whether it is replaced by an energy/scale-dependent modification v/c = F(ξ; E, E_p), and if so specify F explicitly from the deformed boost structure.

Provide a consistent answer to (1)–(3), or prove that no such consistent description exists within the class of DSR theories with a deformed action of the Lorentz group on momentum space.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of how to characterize macroscopic ("DSR") observers and whether the rapidity–velocity relation is deformed remains a recognized open issue in DSR. Later reviews still list this together with the related "soccer ball problem" (recovering standard transformations for macroscopic bodies) as unresolved foundational problems, and recent works continue to investigate consistency of boost transformations and critical rapidities in DSR.

status_evidence.title: Doubly-Special Relativity: Facts, Myths and Some Key Open Issues
status_evidence.snippet: Review identifying open issues in DSR including the description of macroscopic observers and composition of momenta.
status_evidence.claim: The nature of DSR observers and macroscopic-body behavior remain listed as key open issues in DSR.

status_evidence.title: Doubly special relativity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: DSR suffers from several inconsistencies in formulation that have yet to be resolved. Most notably, it is difficult to recover the standard transformation behavior for macroscopic bodies, known as the soccer ball problem.
status_evidence.claim: DSR has unresolved issues regarding macroscopic observers (soccer ball problem).

status_evidence.title: On the Consistency of Covariant Light-Speed Variation in Doubly Special Relativity
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses critical rapidity in DSR within the physically allowed range of deformed boosts.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work still investigates the deformed boost/rapidity structure in DSR, indicating the issue is active.
